description:
FOUND s492b (2026-09-21) while attributing the companion movers of the everyday-Perl batch.
PRE-EXISTING: MEASURED on a 5ce155cb `git archive` extraction and on the s492b tree, the two runs
serial and back to back (scratch/s492b/log-charset-{base,tree}.txt).

  file                       PASS/FAIL base   PASS/FAIL tree   NEW/FIXED rows base   NEW/FIXED tree
  re/charset.t               5224/328         5224/328         104 / 104             104 / 104
  re/regexp_unicode_prop.t   778/332          778/332          173 / 366             155 / 346

The COUNTS are identical on both sides and identical to baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, so no row
changed its verdict; what moves is the row KEY, i.e. the description the test itself prints.

re/charset.t's descriptions are built by `display()` in perl's t/test.pl, which renders a character
either as itself or as `\xNN` depending on `chr $c =~ /[[:print:]]/a` -- and **PCL silently ignores
the /a modifier** (#2092, P15).  So PCL prints the raw byte 0x85 where the blessed key says the four
characters `\x85`, for all 104 of that file's rows.  That makes #2092 the cause of this file's churn,
and the churn will disappear when #2092's /a phase lands -- no separate fix is wanted here.

re/regexp_unicode_prop.t's churn is not constant between two runs of the SAME tree (173/366 vs
155/346), so its descriptions carry an iteration order, exactly the #1082 shape.

WHY IT MATTERS: these rows make every `--all` companion run read "NOT clean" for a reason that is
not a regression -- the same failure mode #1966 had (s494 re-spelled 178 keys for it), and the same
one #1965 / #1082 registered for re/pat.t and four op/ files.  A reader who does not know cannot tell
these apart from a real NEW ROW.

WHAT TO DO (not done here -- this batch only measured it):
  * register both files as *rows-unstable* the way s468be registered the four, so the runner reports
    them as `=` instead of NEW/FIXED; or
  * for re/charset.t, wait for #2092's /a phase and re-measure -- if the descriptions then match the
    blessed keys byte for byte, the file needs no registration at all.  Take that measurement BEFORE
    registering, because a registration hides a file for good.
subject: COMPANION MEASUREMENT (pre-existing): re/charset.t and re/regexp_unicode_prop.t are two more #1082-family ROWS-UNSTABLE files -- their row DESCRIPTIONS redraw every run, so every companion run reports ~104 and ~150-370 NEW/FIXED rows that are not regressions
